title: Worsening cognitive performance is associated with increases in systemic inflammation following hematopoietic cell transplantation
authors: Hoogland AI, Nelson AM, Gonzalez BD, Small BJ, Breen EC, Sutton SK, Syrjala KL, Bower JE, Pidala J, Booth-Jones M, Jacobsen PB, Jim HSL
population: Adults with hematologic malignancies (AML 31%, MDS 18%, NHL 15%, ALL 12%) scheduled for allogeneic HCT; mean age 52; 58% male; 94% Caucasian; assessed pre-HCT and 90 days post-HCT
extraction_notes: Round 1: Extracted 2 edges (IL-6→verbal memory, sTNF-RII→attention). Round 2: Comprehensive extraction of all p<.05 and p<.10 associations from Table 3 linear mixed models (Time x Biomarker interactions). Added 5 new edge evidence rows: CRP→verbal memory (p<.05), CRP→visual memory (p<.05), sTNF-RII→verbal memory (p<.10 trend), IL-6→executive (p<.10 trend), IL-6→attention (p<.10 trend). Added population norms (5 cognitive domain pre-HCT t-scores). Total: 7 edge evidence rows across 3 edges (ER_OIC_EPISODIC×4, ER_OIC_ATTNSUST×2, ER_OIC_EXECPLAN×1), 5 population norm rows. Effect sizes converted from unstandardized betas via beta_std=b*SD_x/SD_y → partial_r → d. ROB=moderate: longitudinal design, good biomarker assays, N=85, but no healthy control group and HCT population may not generalize to solid tumor CRCI.
